title: The lowest place (Luke 14:7–14)
hookLine: sit at the bottom of the table, and invite those who can't repay
carry: invite the ones who can't repay

lines: A SEATING CHART BY THE DOOR.
GUESTS ANGLING FOR THE BEST SEATS.
cards: A wedding reception, and a seating chart on an easel by the door. Table one, near the couple: family and the best friends. Table twelve, by the kitchen door: the coworkers and the plus-ones nobody's met.

And at least one guest quietly moves a place card. Jesus is at a sabbath dinner in the house of a leading Pharisee, watching the guests do exactly this: angling for the first seats. So he gives them some advice.

teach.b: First, to the guests. Don't grab the top seat, he says. Someone more honored may arrive, the host will ask you to move, and you'll walk the whole room to the bottom in front of everybody.
"But when thou art invited, go, sit down in the lowest place."

Then the host may say: friend, go up higher, and you'll be honored before the whole table. It sounds like good manners, and it is. The Book of Proverbs gives almost the same advice about standing before a king.
But Jesus ends with a line that goes past manners: "every one that exalteth himself, shall be humbled; and he that humbleth himself, shall be exalted." Then he turns to the host.
When you give a dinner, don't invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives or your rich neighbors, because they'll invite you back, and that's your repayment.

teach.h: CALL THE POOR, THE LAME, THE BLIND.
teach.b: Instead: "call the poor, the maimed, the lame, and the blind; And thou shalt be blessed, because they have not wherewith to make thee recompense." That's the harder half.
You invite me, I invite you, and the account is settled. Jesus says: break the loop. Invite the people who can't pay you back, and let God do the repaying, at the resurrection of the just.
The two halves fit. As a guest, don't measure your worth by your seat. As a host, don't measure your guests by what they can give.

teach.h: SIT DOWN IN THE LOWEST PLACE.
teach.b: The lowest place isn't a trick for getting promoted. It's a way of sitting at a table where nobody is keeping score.

how: Some Catholic parishes and communities, such as the Catholic Worker and the Community of Sant'Egidio, hold meals where the poor sit at the table as guests, not only as people being served food.

o: the seat kept for the host at a dinner
the final spot in a race or a contest
the lowest seat, taken without angling

games.q: at the Pharisee's dinner — tap the pairs.

s: Jesus' seating advice has a close parallel in Proverbs
Proverbs 25 advises not to put yourself forward before a king.
Jesus told hosts to invite friends who will invite them back
he said invite those who can't repay, and you'll be blessed.
this teaching happened at a Pharisee's sabbath dinner
Luke 14:1 sets it in the house of a leading Pharisee.

games.q: you arrive at a big dinner. the best seats near the host are still empty. where do you sit?
o: near the host, before someone else takes it.
games.why: Jesus says sit in the lowest place, so the host may say friend, go up higher, and you'll be honored.

practice: Think through today's rooms, a meeting, a meal, a line, a group chat, and where you'd usually take the better place: the first word, the best chair, the last slice, the credit.
Picture taking the lower one instead, on purpose and quietly. If you pray, ask for a humble heart.

wordCard.voice: Last place. Jesus' advice at a dinner: take the bottom seat, and when you host, invite the ones who can't repay. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: the last place, the lowest seat at the table.

carryVoice: Your line: invite the ones who can't repay. A seat at the table, and no account to settle. Until tomorrow.
